question.problem: A tree sapling grows by $2$ centimeters per day. Assuming that one year has $365$ days, how many meters does the tree grow in one year?
question.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

One of the conversion factors should change $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

The other conversion factor should change $\text{day}$ into $\text{year}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{year}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}\cdot \frac{\text{days}}{\text{year}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}.$

- There are $100$ centimeters in one meter, therefore, there are $\frac{1}{100}$ meters in one centimeter.

- There are $365$ days in one year.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}} & =2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{1}{100}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}\cdot 365\,\frac{\text{days}}{\text{year}} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{100}\cdot 365(\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{year}}) \\  & =7.3\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $2$ centimeters per day is equivalent to $7.3$ meters per year. In one year, the tree grows by $7.3$ meters.
